protectedChangeRequires: test update in the same change

features.title: Authentication and session ownership
features.summary: Supabase Auth, server-validated bearer tokens, RLS-backed ownership, and single-active-device session replacement.
invariants: Supabase Auth is the only user authentication provider.
Protected backend routes validate the Supabase bearer token server-side.
Ownership is enforced by RLS and user-scoped queries, not by the client.
Single-active-device session replacement is intentional.
Auth state changes must not unmount a live transcription session without cleanup.

features.title: Transcription FSM and reconciliation
features.summary: The browser VAD/Whisper state machine, speculative text handling, Whisper truth-ledger merging, and recovery behavior.
invariants: Browser speech is speculative; Whisper is the truth ledger.
Invalid FSM transitions return the previous state.
WHISPER_COMPLETE merges browser and Whisper text and returns to LISTENING.
Recovery is FAILED -> RECOVERING -> LISTENING.
SESSION_END clears speculative text and the active trace ID.
Token-level reconciliation must not drop or duplicate committed text.

features.title: Audio capture and playback lifecycle
features.summary: Microphone consent, VAD, audio ring buffer, barge-in, Polly playback, device preferences, and cleanup.
invariants: Microphone access is user-initiated and consent-gated.
Workers, audio nodes, media streams, timers, and subscriptions are released on teardown.
Barge-in must not leave two playback paths active.
Device preferences are applied before the next session starts.
Long-running audio work stays out of synchronous Lambda requests.

features.title: Conversation modes and mock exams
features.summary: Standard interview, practice, study, and mock-exam flows, including English reading/writing stages and exam review.
invariants: Mode changes do not lose persisted history or corrupt the active exam run.
Mock-exam reading/writing stages and stable prompt selections are preserved.
Mock-exam review is server-generated; the client does not invent scores.
Standard interview, practice, and study modes preserve their turn semantics.

features.title: Civics grading and turn policy
features.summary: Server-authoritative civics grading, answer matching, confirmations, hints, repeats, progress questions, and question-bank routing.
invariants: Civics answers are graded server-side.
Partial answers, confirmations, hints, repeats, progress questions, and ungraded current-answer questions remain distinct.
graded_answers is the authoritative record for progress reports.
A grading change requires an eval run and a reviewed prompt change.
Question-bank IDs and test-version routing remain stable.

features.title: Progress reports and daily learning
features.summary: Daily progress report aggregation from persisted messages and graded answers, including Bedrock generation and upsert.
invariants: Reports are generated from persisted messages and authoritative graded answers.
The Lambda never overrides recorded verdicts with model judgment.
A session with no messages and no graded answers returns an empty report without calling Bedrock.
The report includes the educational disclaimer and is upserted by (user_id, date).
Bedrock or database failures return a typed error, not a fabricated report.

features.title: History persistence and pagination
features.summary: Conversation persistence, ordered history loading, infinite scroll, and transcript download.
invariants: Messages remain ordered and are never dropped or duplicated by pagination.
History is user-scoped and RLS-protected.
Loading older messages preserves scroll position and the active session.
Transcript download reflects the persisted conversation.

features.title: Settings and preferences
features.summary: User settings persistence for theme, font size, language, voice, audio devices, notifications, and accessibility.
invariants: Settings persist per user and survive reloads.
Theme and font-size previews do not commit until saved.
Language, voice, audio-device, notification, and accessibility preference keys remain stable.
Invalid or missing settings fall back to documented defaults.

features.title: Internationalization and RTL
features.summary: English, Spanish, French, and Arabic localization, RTL layout, and language persistence.
invariants: English, Spanish, French, and Arabic remain supported.
Arabic renders RTL; layout, icons, and overlays respect direction.
New user-facing strings live in locale files, not components.
Language changes persist and do not reset the active session.

features.title: Accessibility and responsive layout
features.summary: Semantic controls, keyboard access, focus management, reduced motion, touch targets, and responsive desktop/mobile layouts.
invariants: Interactive controls are semantic, labelled, keyboard reachable, and have visible focus.
Modals trap focus, restore focus on close, and close on Escape where appropriate.
Layout works at narrow and wide widths without horizontal overflow.
Reduced-motion preferences are respected.
Touch targets remain usable on mobile.

features.title: Account settings and deletion
features.summary: Profile and password updates plus authenticated, cascading account deletion.
invariants: Profile and password updates are authenticated and user-scoped.
Account deletion requires a valid bearer token and deletes only the caller.
Deletion uses the service-role key server-side only.
Deletion failures return a safe error and do not claim success.
Cascade deletion removes user-owned data.

features.title: Notifications and feedback
features.summary: User-scoped notifications, read state, notification preferences, and feedback submission.
invariants: Notifications are user-scoped and respect notification preferences.
Read/unread and clear-all state remain consistent.
Feedback submission does not expose transcripts or PII beyond the intended payload.
Feedback failures are visible to the user, not swallowed.

features.title: API contracts and backend functions
features.summary: The three API Gateway routes, their request/response contracts, auth behavior, and Lambda boundaries.
invariants: Routes remain POST /transcript, POST /complete-session, and POST /delete-account.
Request/response shapes and status codes are contracts.
Every protected route validates the bearer token before work.
Invalid input returns 400; missing/invalid auth returns 401; downstream failure returns 500.
Backend handlers remain raw API Gateway handlers; no Express layer.

features.title: Database schema and RLS
features.summary: Supabase migrations, RLS policies, constraints, indexes, and generated-type alignment.
invariants: Migrations are the only schema source of truth. The baseline records the existing hosted schema; later migrations advance it.
Schema changes are expand/contract and include a rollback plan.
Every user-owned table has RLS enabled and owner-scoped policies. No policy is unconditional or explicitly targets anon.
Anon has no EXECUTE on public functions; SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path; trigger-only helpers revoke EXECUTE.
Foreign keys to auth.users cascade on delete.
Every public table except sessions keeps NOT NULL created_at/updated_at with an on-update trigger.
Generated TypeScript types and docs/DATABASE.md stay in sync with migrations.
The live round-trip test remains available behind RUN_DB_ROUNDTRIP=1.

features.title: Security and privacy boundaries
features.summary: Secret handling, server-side authorization, input validation, log redaction, and safe error responses.
invariants: Secrets never enter VITE_* variables, client code, logs, tests, or commits.
Authorization is enforced server-side and by RLS.
Public database objects are deny-by-default: no anon table access to user data and no anon EXECUTE on public functions.
Maintenance RPCs such as purge_old_messages are not callable by clients.
Logs exclude tokens, raw authorization headers, transcripts, and unnecessary PII.
External input is validated at the boundary.
Error responses do not leak stack traces or secrets.

features.title: Observability and error handling
features.summary: Structured logging, correlation context, error boundaries, typed API errors, and loading/retry states.
invariants: Errors are logged with operation and correlation context, not raw payloads.
The error boundary renders a recovery path instead of a blank screen.
API failures surface a typed error and a user-visible message.
Loading, empty, error, and retry states remain distinct.
